html:
The Arrohateck were a small Algonquian-speaking people on the James River in Virginia, just below the falls where Richmond now stands. They belonged to the Powhatan paramount chiefdom, which united some thirty peoples of the coastal plain.

In May 1607, days after the English landed at Jamestown, Christopher Newport and John Smith sailed upriver and were welcomed at the Arrohateck town. In the wars that followed between the English and the Powhatan, the Arrohateck lost their land, and they disappear from records by the mid 1600s. See also Virginia.
